e-9090.knowledge_point: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix
e-9090.problem:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(A^T)$ for every matrix $A?$

- $\text{Null}(A)$

- $\text{Col}(A)$

- $\text{Null}(A^T)$
e-9090.worked_solution:
Recall that $\text{Col}(A^T)$ is the row space of $A,$ and consists of all linear combinations of the rows of $A.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of $A,$ it must be orthogonal to each row of $A.$
But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by $A,$ we multiply each row of $A$ by that vector.
So, $\text{Col}(A^T)$ must be orthogonal to the null space of $A,$ which is $\text{Null}(A).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

**Note:** In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/de22dd5b352e1d5be48f4b6ed3b2a4657ae623c1bd288d3464559758ea334af7.png)

e-9104.knowledge_point: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action
e-9104.problem: Let $A$ be a $m \times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\text{Col}(A^T)$ under the action of $A?$
e-9104.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $A$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/4c69fb7131661c59cec0d5ffc843fe8c89df497c5adb3ed804e0650917dafe1c.png)

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A$ must be $\text{Col}(A),$ the column space of $A.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(A)$ is mapped to the zero vector $\mathbf{0}$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}(A^T)$ must be $\text{Col}(A).$

This can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/8b08bdf79d53f312cabd665bcd4669795bd8851dfb33d5e5db6178bd80b24398.png)

e-9099.knowledge_point: Finding the Dimensions of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix
e-9099.problem: Consider a $8 \times 6$ matrix $A.$ If $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A)) = 3,$ then find $\text{dim}(\text{Col}(A^T)).$
e-9099.worked_solution:
The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/889b83fadd26b377c4dd34143c9b16541630c04e90de3d9b005e7147ead75ad5.png)

In our case, we are given that $m=8,$ $n=6,$ and $n-r=3.$ 

Substituting $n=6$ into $n-r=3,$ we can find the rank of $A{:}$

$$
6 - r = 3 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
r = 3
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{dim}(\text{Col}({A}^{T})) & =r=3.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m\times n$ matrices. What is the image of $\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ under the action of $A+B?$
after.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $A+B$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A+B:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ (a+b)_{1} & (a+b)_{2} & ⋯ & (a+b)_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A+B}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ (a+b)_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $A+B$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B),$ the column space of $A+B.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(A+B)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}((A+B)^{T})=\text{Col}({A}^{T}+{B}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(A+B).$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Let $B$ be a $m\times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ under the action of $B?$
after.worked_solution:
Pre-multiplying a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ by $B$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $B:$

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}| & | & ⋯ & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & ⋯ & {b}_{n} \\ | & | & ⋯ & |\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{B}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ ⋮ \\ {x}_{n}\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {b}_{1} \\ |\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {b}_{2} \\ |\end{aligned}]+⋯+{x}_{n}[\begin{aligned}| \\ {b}_{n} \\ |\end{aligned}]
$$

Therefore, the image of ${R}^{n}$ under the action of $B$ must be $\text{Col}(B),$ the column space of $B.$

Furthermore, since $\text{Null}(B)$ is mapped to the zero vector $0$ by the definition of the null subspace, the image of its orthogonal complement $\text{Col}({B}^{T})$ must be $\text{Col}(B).$

EXPLANATION

The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix A can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

In our case, we are given that m=3, n=4, and m−r=2.

Substituting m=3 into m−r=2, we can find the rank of A:

(3)−r=2⟹r=1

Therefore, we obtain

dim(Col(A))=r=1.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14093810/assets/889b83fadd26b377c4dd34143c9b16541630c04e90de3d9b005e7147ead75ad5.png)

In our case, we are given that $m=3,$ $n=4,$ and $m-r=2.$ 

Substituting $m=3$ into $m-r=2,$ we can find the rank of $A:$

$$
(3)-r=2\,⟹\,r=1
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{dim}(\text{Col}(A)) & =r=1.\end{aligned}
$$
